propose.text: Northwind Supply sells grocery and household goods to businesses. Sales reps take sales_orders from customers, each order has order_lines for products, shipped orders are invoiced in invoices and settled by payments. inventory_snapshots keeps weekly stock counts. Key tables: sales_orders, order_lines, customers, products, invoices, payments, inventory_snapshots.

evidence: deploy/demo-business.sql: schema header and CREATE TABLE statements

summary.text: Northwind Supply sells groceries and household goods to retail, wholesale, hospitality and online customers across five regions. Sales reps take orders, invoices follow shipped orders, and customers pay by bank transfer, card or cheque. Revenue comes from order lines.

facts_told.text: Orders have five statuses: open, shipped, delivered, cancelled, returned.
Customers are one of four segments: Retail, Wholesale, Hospitality, Online.
Wholesale invoices are due after 45 days, all others after 30 days.

inferences.text: Revenue is counted net of line discounts.

people.role: Sales rep: covers a region and manages customer accounts

vocabulary.text: Segment: customer type (Retail, Wholesale, Hospitality, Online).

priorities.text: Overdue invoices and bad debt: some invoices are never paid.

recurring_work.text: Weekly inventory snapshot of units on hand per product.

open_questions.text: Is revenue meant to be net of line discounts?

propose.text: One row per sales region of the business, five in total. Reference data that customers and sales reps point to.

columns.id: Region identifier. Referenced by sales_reps.region_id and customers.region_id.
columns.name: Region name. Values: North, South, East, West, Central. Unique. Use it to label regional breakdowns.

evidence: deploy/demo-business.sql: CREATE TABLE regions and its seed insert

propose.text: One row per sales representative, with the region they cover and whether they are still employed. Customers are assigned to reps through customers.rep_id.

columns.id: Sales rep identifier. Referenced by customers.rep_id.
columns.full_name: Rep display name (personal data). Use it for labels only, never to identify a person.
columns.region_id: Region the rep covers. Joins to regions.id.
columns.hired_on: Date the rep was hired. A business date with no time zone.
columns.is_active: True while the rep is employed and takes customers. False for reps who have left. Count active reps with is_active.

propose.text: One row per customer account (a business that buys goods). Active customers are those with is_active true. Segment and region are the usual ways to group customers.

columns.id: Customer identifier. Referenced by sales_orders.customer_id and invoices.customer_id.
columns.name: Customer business name (personal data if a sole trader). Label only.
columns.segment: Customer type. Values: Retail (shops), Wholesale (bulk buyers, 45-day invoice terms), Hospitality (hotels and restaurants), Online (web retailers). Exactly one per customer.
columns.region_id: Region the customer belongs to. Joins to regions.id. Use it for regional order counts.
columns.rep_id: Sales rep who manages the customer. Joins to sales_reps.id. NULL means no rep is assigned.
columns.city: City of the customer. Free-text location label, not a controlled list.
columns.credit_limit: Maximum unpaid balance allowed for the customer, in the single business currency (units, not cents).
columns.created_at: Date the customer account was created. A business date with no time zone.
columns.is_active: True for customers who can still order. False for closed or lapsed accounts. Count active customers with is_active.

propose.text: One row per product SKU sold, with list price and unit cost. Discontinued products stay in the table because old orders refer to them.

columns.id: Product identifier. Referenced by order_lines.product_id and inventory_snapshots.product_id.
columns.sku: Stock keeping unit code, unique per product, for example SKU-0001 (example).
columns.name: Product display name, category word plus an item number.
columns.category: Product family. Values: Beverages, Cleaning, Dairy, Dry Goods, Frozen, Packaging, Produce, Snacks. Use it for category revenue breakdowns.
columns.unit_price: Current list price per unit, in the business currency units. The price actually charged is on order_lines.unit_price.
columns.unit_cost: Cost per unit to the business, same currency units. Margin is price minus cost.
columns.is_discontinued: True when the product is no longer sold. Count discontinued products with is_discontinued.

propose.text: One row per sales order, the order header. order_date is the business date for reporting. Revenue and order trends exclude status cancelled, and open orders are those not yet shipped.

columns.id: Order identifier. Referenced by order_lines.order_id and invoices.order_id.
columns.customer_id: Customer who placed the order. Joins to customers.id. Use it to reach segment and region.
columns.order_date: Date the order was placed. A business date with no time zone. Use it to place an order in a day, week or month.
columns.status: Order lifecycle stage. Values: open (taken, not yet shipped), shipped (sent, not yet confirmed delivered), delivered (received), cancelled (never revenue), returned (sent back).
columns.channel: How the order arrived. Values: field_sales (rep visit), phone, web, marketplace (third-party site).

evidence: deploy/demo-business.sql: CREATE TABLE sales_orders (status and channel CHECK)

propose.text: One row per product line on a sales order. Line amount is qty * unit_price * (1 - discount_pct / 100). Sum line amounts to get order value and revenue.

columns.order_id: Order this line belongs to. Joins to sales_orders.id.
columns.product_id: Product sold on the line. Joins to products.id.
columns.qty: Units sold on the line. Always above zero. A few bulk orders have hundreds of units.
columns.unit_price: Price per unit actually charged, in business currency units, before discount. Can differ from products.unit_price when prices changed.
columns.discount_pct: Percentage discount on the line, 0 to 100. 0 means no discount. Only some wholesale lines carry a discount.

propose.text: One row per invoice, issued for a non-cancelled sales order. Amount is the total of that order's lines. Unpaid balance is invoice amount minus the payments recorded against it.

columns.order_id: The sales order this invoice bills. Joins to sales_orders.id. Unique, so one invoice per order.
columns.customer_id: Customer being billed. Joins to customers.id.
columns.invoice_date: Date the invoice was issued, the day after the order date. A business date with no time zone.
columns.due_date: Date payment is due. 45 days after invoice_date for Wholesale customers, otherwise 30 days.
columns.amount: Invoice total in business currency units, tax not modelled. Compare with the sum of payments.amount to find unpaid balance.

propose.text: One row per payment received against an invoice. paid_at is the business date of receipt. Invoices with no payment rows are unpaid.

columns.invoice_id: Invoice this payment settles. Joins to invoices.id.
columns.paid_at: Date the money was received. A business date with no time zone. paid_at minus invoices.due_date is days paid late, negative when early.
columns.amount: Amount received in business currency units. Usually equals the invoice amount, one payment per invoice.
columns.method: How the customer paid. Values: bank_transfer, card, cheque.

propose.text: One row per product per weekly stock count date. Use the latest snapshot_date for current stock. on_hand of zero means a stock-out on that date.

columns.product_id: Product counted. Joins to products.id. Together with snapshot_date it is the primary key.
columns.snapshot_date: Date of the stock count, taken weekly. A business date with no time zone. The newest date is the current stock position.
columns.on_hand: Units in stock on the snapshot date. Never negative. Zero means out of stock.

propose.title: Identifier naming
propose.text: All table and column names are lowercase snake_case and unquoted. Write public.sales_orders or just sales_orders, never a double-quoted PascalCase name. Correct example: SELECT count(*) FROM customers WHERE is_active.

propose.title: Order status values
propose.text: sales_orders.status is open, shipped, delivered, cancelled or returned. Revenue and order trends exclude cancelled. Open means taken but not yet shipped. Counts of cancelled orders use status cancelled.

evidence: deploy/demo-business.sql: invoices are created only for status <> cancelled

propose.title: Money and line amounts
propose.text: All money columns are numeric amounts in one business currency, in whole currency units and not cents. A line amount is qty * unit_price * (1 - discount_pct / 100). Revenue is the sum of line amounts for orders that are not cancelled. Whether revenue should net out discounts is an open question.

evidence: deploy/demo-business.sql: invoices amount derived from order lines

propose.title: Dates have no time zone
propose.text: Every date column is of type date, with no time and no time zone. order_date is the business date of an order, invoice_date and due_date place an invoice, paid_at is the day payment arrived, snapshot_date is the weekly stock count date.

propose.title: Unpaid invoice balance
propose.text: An invoice is unpaid when the sum of its payments.amount is below invoices.amount. Total unpaid balance is the sum of invoices.amount minus the sum of payments.amount. A small share of invoices is never paid and counts as bad debt.

evidence: db: aggregate sums of invoices and payments

propose.title: Current stock is the latest snapshot
propose.text: inventory_snapshots holds weekly history. Current stock for a product is its row with the newest snapshot_date. Summing on_hand across all dates is meaningless.

propose.title: Term: Segment
propose.text: Customer type, stored in customers.segment: Retail, Wholesale, Hospitality or Online. Used to compare buying and payment behaviour. Wholesale has longer invoice terms.

propose.title: Term: Open balance
propose.text: Invoice amount not yet covered by payments: invoices.amount minus the sum of payments.amount for that invoice. Summed over invoices it is the unpaid balance owed to the business.

propose.title: Term: Days late
propose.text: paid_at minus due_date for a payment, in days. Positive means paid after the due date, negative means paid early. Averages by segment show which customers pay slowly.

propose.title: Monthly revenue
propose.text: Sum of qty * unit_price * (1 - discount_pct / 100) over order lines of orders that are not cancelled, per calendar month of order_date. One business currency, whole units. Grain: one value per month. Reference SQL: SELECT to_char(date_trunc('month', o.order_date), 'YYYY-MM') AS month, round(sum(l.qty * l.unit_price * (1 - l.discount_pct / 100)), 2) AS revenue FROM sales_orders o JOIN order_lines l ON l.order_id = o.id WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

kpis.reference_sql: SELECT to_char(date_trunc('month', o.order_date), 'YYYY-MM') AS month, round(sum(l.qty * l.unit_price * (1 - l.discount_pct / 100)), 2) AS revenue FROM sales_orders o JOIN order_lines l ON l.order_id = o.id WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

propose.title: Unpaid invoice balance
propose.text: Sum of invoices.amount minus sum of payments.amount, across all invoices. One business currency, whole units. Grain: a single number as of today, with no date filter. Reference SQL: SELECT round(sum(amount) - (SELECT coalesce(sum(amount), 0) FROM payments), 2) AS unpaid_balance FROM invoices

kpis.reference_sql: SELECT round(sum(amount) - (SELECT coalesce(sum(amount), 0) FROM payments), 2) AS unpaid_balance FROM invoices

propose.title: Average days paid late by segment
propose.text: Average of payments.paid_at minus invoices.due_date, grouped by customers.segment. Grain: one value per segment. Positive means late. Reference SQL: SELECT c.segment, round(avg(p.paid_at - i.due_date), 1) AS avg_days_late FROM payments p JOIN invoices i ON i.id = p.invoice_id JOIN customers c ON c.id = i.customer_id GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

kpis.reference_sql: SELECT c.segment, round(avg(p.paid_at - i.due_date), 1) AS avg_days_late FROM payments p JOIN invoices i ON i.id = p.invoice_id JOIN customers c ON c.id = i.customer_id GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC
evidence: db: average days late by segment aggregate

propose.title: Units on hand
propose.text: Sum of on_hand across all products on the latest snapshot_date. Grain: a single number for the newest weekly stock count. Reference SQL: SELECT sum(on_hand) AS units_on_hand FROM inventory_snapshots WHERE snapshot_date = (SELECT max(snapshot_date) FROM inventory_snapshots)

kpis.reference_sql: SELECT sum(on_hand) AS units_on_hand FROM inventory_snapshots WHERE snapshot_date = (SELECT max(snapshot_date) FROM inventory_snapshots)
evidence: db: sum of on_hand on max(snapshot_date)

watch_candidates.title: Overdue invoice balance above 900000
watch_candidates.condition: Total balance of invoices whose due_date is before today and whose payments are below the invoice amount (invoices.amount minus sum of payments.amount) rises above 900000.
watch_candidates.draft_sql: SELECT round(coalesce(sum(i.amount - coalesce(p.paid, 0)), 0), 2) AS overdue_balance FROM invoices i LEFT JOIN (SELECT invoice_id, sum(amount) AS paid FROM payments GROUP BY invoice_id) p ON p.invoice_id = i.id WHERE i.due_date < current_date AND i.amount > coalesce(p.paid, 0)
watch_candidates.rationale: Overdue money is cash the business is waiting for. When it fires, review slow-paying segments and chase the largest balances.
evidence: db: aggregate run read-only returned one row

watch_candidates.title: Weekly revenue drop of more than 20 percent
watch_candidates.condition: Revenue of the latest 7 days of order_date (qty * unit_price * (1 - discount_pct / 100) on orders that are not cancelled) divided by revenue of the 7 days before falls below 0.8.
watch_candidates.draft_sql: WITH m AS (SELECT max(order_date) AS d FROM sales_orders), r AS (SELECT o.order_date, sum(l.qty * l.unit_price * (1 - l.discount_pct / 100)) AS rev FROM sales_orders o JOIN order_lines l ON l.order_id = o.id WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled' GROUP BY o.order_date) SELECT round((SELECT sum(rev) FROM r, m WHERE r.order_date > m.d - 7) / nullif((SELECT sum(rev) FROM r, m WHERE r.order_date > m.d - 14 AND r.order_date <= m.d - 7), 0), 3) AS revenue_ratio
watch_candidates.rationale: A sharp week-on-week fall can mean a lost customer or channel problem. When it fires, break revenue down by region and segment.
evidence: db: aggregate run read-only returned one row

watch_candidates.title: Products at zero stock in the latest count
watch_candidates.condition: Number of products with on_hand = 0 on the newest snapshot_date of inventory_snapshots rises above 0.
watch_candidates.draft_sql: SELECT count(*) AS zero_stock_products FROM inventory_snapshots WHERE snapshot_date = (SELECT max(snapshot_date) FROM inventory_snapshots) AND on_hand = 0
watch_candidates.rationale: A stock-out means lost sales. When it fires, ask purchasing to reorder those products.
evidence: db: aggregate run read-only returned one row

open_questions.question: Should revenue be net of line discounts, or list value before discount?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Wholesale lines carry discounts, so the two definitions differ and KPIs and dashboards depend on the choice.
open_questions.seen_in_code: deploy/demo-business.sql: invoices.amount is computed with discount_pct applied, so this pack nets discounts out.
